pr_title: Bluetooth: Audio: Media - truncate strings for notification
pr_body:
Truncate strings being notified to fit the ATT_MTU, to prevent
notifications from not being delivered due to being too long.

For now uses the minimum ATT_MTU, as the MCS does not yet track
connections.  (See https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/44176)

Signed-off-by: Asbjørn Sæbø <asbjorn.sabo@nordicsemi.no>

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/42090
pr_comments: Pull request re-opened to fix stuck CI (due to GitHub mishap)

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Audio: MCS BSIM notification length warning
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When running the mcs_mcc.h babblesim tests, it looks like the MTU isn't large to send the application data:

```
d_01: @00:00:19.081741  [00:00:19.081,726] <dbg> bt_mcs: media_proxy_sctrl_track_title_cb: Notifying track title: Interlude #1 (Song for Alison)
d_01: @00:00:19.081741  [00:00:19.081,726] <wrn> bt_att: No ATT channel for MTU 33
d_01: @00:00:19.081741  [00:00:19.081,726] <wrn> bt_gatt: No buffer available to send notification
d_01: @00:00:19.081741  [00:00:19.081,726] <dbg> bt_mcs: notify: Notification error: ENOTCONN (-107)
```

This also means that the remote side, i.e. the client, does not verify the song names in the tests. The server does also not have any GATT MTU requirements similar to the buffer count: 

```c
BUILD_ASSERT(CONFIG_BT_L2CAP_TX_BUF_COUNT >= 10, "Too few L2CAP buffers");
```

**To Reproduce**
Build and run the mcs_mcc.h test

**Expected behavior**
Pass without warnings or errors. 
The client should check for the name notifications
The `BT_MCS_TRACK_TITLE_MAX` should not be above the GATT MTU, or alternatively it should be truncated to fit the MTU when sending (ditto for the other titles). 

**Impact**
Annoyance at this point, but will be a significant issue when this starts to be used. 

**Logs and console output**
See above

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Commit SHA or Version used: d51a67b7c098c8bb5479a7b87f05dc40fb76e065

**Additional context**
N/A

review_comments: Group titles and segment names are kept in the object, not as characteristics.

I'm not see the aforementioned comment in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/41189 :)

> Group titles and segment names are kept in the object, not as characteristics.

Not sure how that relates to the media player name - Can you elaborate?

1) It is a note in the description, not a comment
2) No relation - they are other strings, and I just wanted to show that they are not relevant for this PR.

I have a feeling this should be handled by the stack to send as much as it can depending on MTU.
So once `bt_gatt_notify_uuid` is called it should feed the buffer up to MTU and leave the client with the decision whether it wants to read the rest. Returning error is not sufficient since, the value should be notified anyway, and the Server has no power to exchange the MTU by itself

I disagree. I think it should be up to the individual service determine if a notification should be truncated or not. 

Furthermore, as this PR also demonstrates, we may not always want to naively truncate e.g. UTF8 encoded strings either, as that would essentially send improperly encoded strings.

I think Emil is correct.  What to do with notifications may be service-specific, and we do not want to put that kind of information into the stack.
- service-specific information does not belong in the general stack
- it is complicated to get it there - the notify would also have to include some kind of type information

In this case, what is truncated is track titles (later also player names), and those can well serve their purpose even if truncated - they will typically just be shown to the user.
